array-frames.quote: At each source, gate and sink $v$, assign an invertible $R$-linear operator $D_v$ on $R^\Omega$, called its frame.

array-frames.name: input frame
array-frames.meaning: The direct sum of the source frames over the input roles.
array-frames.quote: It holds at the sources by definition: with $D_{\rm in}=\bigoplus_w D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}$ stacking the source frames over the input roles $w$, a physical input $f$ is interpreted as the logical input $g=D_{\rm in}^{-1}f$, which needs no preprocessing.

array-frames.name: output frame
array-frames.meaning: The direct sum of the sink frames over the output roles.
array-frames.quote: With $D_{\rm out}=\bigoplus_w D_{\mathrm{sink}(w)}$, the implemented operator is therefore

array-frames.name: role permutation
array-frames.meaning: The map sending each input role to its output role.
array-frames.quote: So if the scalar network is a signed role permutation sending input role $w$ to output role $\rho(w)$ with scalar sign $\varepsilon_w$, that route applies $\varepsilon_wD_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}^{-1}$ to its input array.

array-frames.name: route sign
array-frames.meaning: The scalar sign of the route from input role w.
array-frames.quote: So if the scalar network is a signed role permutation sending input role $w$ to output role $\rho(w)$ with scalar sign $\varepsilon_w$, that route applies $\varepsilon_wD_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}^{-1}$ to its input array.

array-frames.name: gate fan-in
array-frames.meaning: The number of input arrays of a gate.
array-frames.quote: At a gate $G$ with $t$ input arrays, every incoming array has the common frame $D_v$, and a gate output combines the logical inputs $\varphi_1,\dots,\varphi_t$ with coefficients $c_j\in R$.

butterfly.name: transform length
butterfly.meaning: The length of the transform, a power of two.
butterfly.quote: Take input values $z_k$ at positions $0\le k<t$, where $t$ is the transform length, a power of two.

butterfly.name: input value
butterfly.meaning: The input value at position k.
butterfly.quote: Take input values $z_k$ at positions $0\le k<t$, where $t$ is the transform length, a power of two.

butterfly.name: twiddle root
butterfly.meaning: The primitive t-th root of unity e^{2 pi i/t}.
butterfly.quote: The transform is $(F_tz)_m=\frac1t\sum_{j=0}^{t-1} z_j\omega_t^{-jm}$, where $\omega_t=e^{2\pi i/t}$, $m$ is the output index and $j$ runs over input positions.

butterfly.name: output index
butterfly.meaning: The index of an output of the transform.
butterfly.quote: The transform is $(F_tz)_m=\frac1t\sum_{j=0}^{t-1} z_j\omega_t^{-jm}$, where $\omega_t=e^{2\pi i/t}$, $m$ is the output index and $j$ runs over input positions.

butterfly.name: input position
butterfly.meaning: The summation index running over input positions.
butterfly.quote: The transform is $(F_tz)_m=\frac1t\sum_{j=0}^{t-1} z_j\omega_t^{-jm}$, where $\omega_t=e^{2\pi i/t}$, $m$ is the output index and $j$ runs over input positions.

butterfly.name: lowest bit
butterfly.meaning: The lowest bit of the output index m.
butterfly.quote: Write $m=2h+b$, where $b\in\{0,1\}$ is the lowest bit of $m$ and $h$ is the remaining index (on this page $h$ is not the ground-set size or wrap indicator of earlier pages).

butterfly.name: butterfly
butterfly.meaning: The two-point averaging and differencing step.
butterfly.quote: A butterfly is the two-point step $H_0(u,v)=(\frac{u+v}{2},\frac{u-v}{2})$ applied to a pair of values $u,v$.

butterfly.name: remaining index
butterfly.meaning: The index m with its lowest bit removed.
butterfly.quote: Write $m=2h+b$, where $b\in\{0,1\}$ is the lowest bit of $m$ and $h$ is the remaining index (on this page $h$ is not the ground-set size or wrap indicator of earlier pages).

chirp.name: position
chirp.meaning: A position in an array, one index per axis.
chirp.quote: Arrays have $d$ axes and are indexed by positions $\boldsymbol j=(j_1,\dots,j_d)$.

chirp.name: axis lengths
chirp.meaning: The tuple of the even axis lengths.
chirp.quote: The tuple $\boldsymbol t=(t_1,\dots,t_d)$ lists the axis lengths, each even,

chirp.name: coprime multiplier
chirp.meaning: An integer coprime to the axis length t_i.
chirp.quote: and $s_i$ is an integer coprime to $t_i$.

chirp.name: input position
chirp.meaning: An input position of the transform.
chirp.quote: where $\boldsymbol k$ runs over input positions and $\boldsymbol f=(f_1,\dots,f_d)$ is the frequency labelling an output entry.

chirp.name: frequency
chirp.meaning: The frequency labelling an output entry.
chirp.quote: where $\boldsymbol k$ runs over input positions and $\boldsymbol f=(f_1,\dots,f_d)$ is the frequency labelling an output entry.

chirp.name: normalized transform
chirp.meaning: The normalized discrete Fourier transform with axis lengths t.
chirp.quote: The normalized transform $F_{\boldsymbol t}$ is given by $(F_{\boldsymbol t}u)_{\boldsymbol f}=\frac1T\sum_{\boldsymbol k}u_{\boldsymbol k}\exp(-2\pi i\sum_i k_if_i/t_i)$, where $\boldsymbol k$ runs over input positions and $\boldsymbol f=(f_1,\dots,f_d)$ is the frequency labelling an output entry.

chirp.name: target permutation
chirp.meaning: The permutation of the output that puts at position j the entry of frequency (-s_i j_i)_i.
chirp.quote: Gaussian resampling leaves a target permutation $Q$, a reordering of the output of a power-of-two transform; the identity absorbs $Q$ into a convolution, so it is never executed as a sort

chirp.name: chirp
chirp.meaning: The chirp, a phase quadratic in the position.
chirp.quote: Define the chirp $a_{\boldsymbol j}=\exp\left(-\pi i\sum_{i=1}^d s_ij_i^2/t_i\right)$ and let $\overline a$ be its complex conjugate. This $a$ is not a bank index.

conjecture.name: bit length
conjecture.meaning: The number of bits in each of the two integers being multiplied.
conjecture.quote: The Schönhage–Strassen optimality conjecture is the claim that $n\log n$ is the best possible order of growth for the time to multiply two integers, where $n$ is the number of bits in each; it is the statement that the main result of this wiki disproves.

conjecture.name: power saving
conjecture.meaning: A fixed positive constant, the amount by which the exponent of the logarithm is lowered.
conjecture.quote: Its running time is $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$, where $\kappa>0$ is a fixed constant, the amount by which the exponent of the logarithm is lowered.

contraction-maps.name: linear map
contraction-maps.meaning: A linear map whose norm bound is being defined.
contraction-maps.quote: A linear map $L$ is a *contraction* if $\|Lu\|\le\|u\|$ for every $u$.

contraction-maps.name: bilinear map
contraction-maps.meaning: A map linear in each of its two operands.
contraction-maps.quote: A map $\mathcal M(f,g)$ that is linear in each operand $f$ and $g$ separately is a *bilinear contraction* if $\|\mathcal M(f,g)\|\le\|f\|\,\|g\|$.

contraction-maps.name: computed input
contraction-maps.meaning: The computed input that replaces the exact input u.
contraction-maps.quote: Suppose a computed input $u'$ replaces the exact input $u$.

contraction-maps.name: computed first operand
contraction-maps.quote: For a bilinear contraction, replace operands $f,g$ by $f',g'$.

contraction-maps.name: computed second operand
contraction-maps.quote: For a bilinear contraction, replace operands $f,g$ by $f',g'$.

contraction-maps.name: normalized transform
contraction-maps.meaning: The normalized discrete Fourier transform on sequences of q entries.
contraction-maps.quote: where $F_q$ is the transform on sequences of $q$ entries.

contraction-maps.name: first operand
contraction-maps.meaning: The first operand of the bilinear map.
contraction-maps.quote: A map $\mathcal M(f,g)$ that is linear in each operand $f$ and $g$ separately is a *bilinear contraction* if $\|\mathcal M(f,g)\|\le\|f\|\,\|g\|$.

contraction-maps.name: second operand
contraction-maps.meaning: The second operand of the bilinear map.
contraction-maps.quote: A map $\mathcal M(f,g)$ that is linear in each operand $f$ and $g$ separately is a *bilinear contraction* if $\|\mathcal M(f,g)\|\le\|f\|\,\|g\|$.

controlled-shifts.name: prime radix
controlled-shifts.meaning: The radix of the stored digits, a prime (not a sequence length).
controlled-shifts.quote: Fix a prime $q$, the radix of the stored digits; this $q$ is a prime radix, not a sequence length as on the cyclic convolution and discrete Fourier transform pages.

controlled-shifts.name: field digit count
controlled-shifts.meaning: The number of base-q digits of a field.
controlled-shifts.quote: Let $b\ge1$ be the number of base-$q$ digits of a field; this $b$ is not the lowest bit of an output index as on the butterfly page.

controlled-shifts.name: field value count
controlled-shifts.meaning: The number of values a field can take.
controlled-shifts.quote: Put $Q=q^b$, the number of values a field can take.

controlled-shifts.name: field value
controlled-shifts.meaning: The value of the target field, an integer from 0 to Q-1 (not the ring variable).
controlled-shifts.quote: The target field has value $y\in\{0,\dots,Q-1\}$; here $y$ is a field value, not the ring variable.

controlled-shifts.name: offset
controlled-shifts.meaning: The offset added to the target field, prepared from the control values.
controlled-shifts.quote: where $a$ is the offset prepared from the control values; this $a$ is not a bank index.

controlled-shifts.name: suffix digit count
controlled-shifts.meaning: The number of digits following the target field.
controlled-shifts.quote: Let $B$ be the number of digits that follow the target; this $B$ is not the number of entries per row on the stream-operations page.

controlled-shifts.name: scaling multiplier
controlled-shifts.meaning: A fixed positive integer prime to q by which the field is multiplied.
controlled-shifts.quote: Let $c$ be a fixed positive integer prime to $q$.

controlled-shifts.name: wrap count
controlled-shifts.meaning: The number of times cy wraps past Q.
controlled-shifts.quote: where $j=\lfloor cy/Q\rfloor$ is the number of times $cy$ wraps past $Q$; this $j$ is not a digit value as on the stream-operations page.

controlled-shifts.name: scaled position
controlled-shifts.meaning: The position cy - jQ to which the block at position y is sent.
controlled-shifts.quote: The map $y\mapsto cy \pmod Q$ sends the block at position $y$ to position $y'=cy-jQ$, where $j=\lfloor cy/Q\rfloor$ is the number of times $cy$ wraps past $Q$; this $j$ is not a digit value as on the stream-operations page.

controlled-shifts.name: unit denominator
controlled-shifts.meaning: The positive integer denominator of a rational unit, prime to q.
controlled-shifts.quote: A rational unit is a signed ratio $c/c'$ of positive integers $c,c'$ both prime to $q$.

convolution.name: sequence length
convolution.meaning: The number of entries in each sequence being convolved.
convolution.quote: For two sequences $f,g$ indexed by $\mathbb Z/q\mathbb Z$, where $q$ is the number of entries in each sequence, the cyclic convolution is

convolution.name: axis count
convolution.meaning: The number of axes of the underlying cyclic convolution.
convolution.quote: Here $d$ is the number of axes of the underlying cyclic convolution, and $t_i$ is the length of axis $i$.

convolution.name: axis length
convolution.meaning: The number of addresses along cyclic axis i.
convolution.quote: Here $d$ is the number of axes of the underlying cyclic convolution, and $t_i$ is the length of axis $i$.

convolution.name: address count
convolution.meaning: The number of addresses of an array, the product of the axis lengths.
convolution.quote: Let $M=\prod_{i<d}t_i$ be the number of addresses, and $T=rM$ the number of complex coefficients in an array.

convolution.name: coefficient count
convolution.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in an array.
convolution.quote: Let $M=\prod_{i<d}t_i$ be the number of addresses, and $T=rM$ the number of complex coefficients in an array.

convolution.name: index permutation
convolution.meaning: A permutation of the indices of an array.
convolution.quote: Write $\pi$ for a permutation of the indices, $F$ for the normalized Fourier transform of length $q$, and $F^+$ for the transform with the opposite sign in the exponent.

convolution.name: Fourier transform
convolution.meaning: The normalized discrete Fourier transform of length q.
convolution.quote: Write $\pi$ for a permutation of the indices, $F$ for the normalized Fourier transform of length $q$, and $F^+$ for the transform with the opposite sign in the exponent.

convolution.name: opposite transform
convolution.meaning: The Fourier transform with the opposite sign in the exponent.
convolution.quote: Write $\pi$ for a permutation of the indices, $F$ for the normalized Fourier transform of length $q$, and $F^+$ for the transform with the opposite sign in the exponent.

cost-accounting.name: array volume
cost-accounting.meaning: The number of bits stored when the T coefficients carry Theta(p) bits each, V=Tp=Theta(n).
cost-accounting.quote: Let $V=Tp=\Theta(n)$, the number of stored bits when $T$ coefficients carry $\Theta(p)$ bits each.

cost-accounting.name: margin
cost-accounting.meaning: The amount by which the exponent of p in the i-th dominant cost lies below one.
cost-accounting.quote: Dividing by $V$, seven operations dominate, each a power $p^{1-g_i}$ with margin $g_i>0$ below one.

cost-accounting.name: visit exponent
cost-accounting.meaning: A fixed exponent such that the recursions make at most p^A visits in total.
cost-accounting.quote: Fix an exponent $A$ with at most $p^A$ visits in total, and an exponent $C$ with descriptor setup of at most $p^C$ steps per visit.

cost-accounting.name: setup exponent
cost-accounting.meaning: A fixed exponent bounding the descriptor setup per visit by p^C steps.
cost-accounting.quote: Fix an exponent $A$ with at most $p^A$ visits in total, and an exponent $C$ with descriptor setup of at most $p^C$ steps per visit.

cost-accounting.name: call volume
cost-accounting.meaning: The volume of one packed change of basis.
cost-accounting.quote: Let $V_{\rm call}$ be the volume of one packed change of basis.

crt-map.name: axis count
crt-map.meaning: The number of prime cyclic axes, with no coefficient axis counted.
crt-map.quote: Let $d$ be the number of axes (unlike on the [Cyclic convolution](convolution.md) page, no coefficient axis is counted), let $i$ index them, let $s_i$ be the length of axis $i$, the lengths being pairwise coprime, and let $S=s_1\cdots s_d$.

crt-map.name: axis index
crt-map.meaning: The index of an axis, from 1 to d.
crt-map.quote: Let $d$ be the number of axes (unlike on the [Cyclic convolution](convolution.md) page, no coefficient axis is counted), let $i$ index them, let $s_i$ be the length of axis $i$, the lengths being pairwise coprime, and let $S=s_1\cdots s_d$.

crt-map.name: axis length
crt-map.meaning: The length of source axis i, pairwise coprime with the other axis lengths.
crt-map.quote: Let $d$ be the number of axes (unlike on the [Cyclic convolution](convolution.md) page, no coefficient axis is counted), let $i$ index them, let $s_i$ be the length of axis $i$, the lengths being pairwise coprime, and let $S=s_1\cdots s_d$.

crt-map.name: prefix product
crt-map.meaning: The product of the lengths of the axes before axis i.
crt-map.quote: Let $P_i=\prod_{j<i}s_j$ be the product of the lengths of the axes before axis $i$, and $\mu_i=P_i^{-1}\pmod{s_i}$.

crt-map.name: exponent
crt-map.meaning: The inverse of P_i modulo s_i, the exponent of x_i in the image of x.
crt-map.quote: Let $P_i=\prod_{j<i}s_j$ be the product of the lengths of the axes before axis $i$, and $\mu_i=P_i^{-1}\pmod{s_i}$.

crt-map.name: address map
crt-map.meaning: The algebra isomorphism from the cyclic ring of length S to the product of cyclic rings on the axes, sending x to the product of x_i^{mu_i}.
crt-map.quote: Define $\Phi:\mathbb C[x]/(x^S-1)\to\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_i^{s_i}-1)$ by $x\mapsto\prod_i x_i^{\mu_i}$, with one variable $x_i$ per axis.

crt-map.name: axis variable
crt-map.meaning: The polynomial variable of axis i.
crt-map.quote: Define $\Phi:\mathbb C[x]/(x^S-1)\to\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_i^{s_i}-1)$ by $x\mapsto\prod_i x_i^{\mu_i}$, with one variable $x_i$ per axis.

crt-map.name: mixed-radix digit
crt-map.meaning: The digit of the coefficient index k in position j, with 0 <= a_j < s_j.
crt-map.quote: Write $k=\sum_ja_jP_j$ in mixed radix, with digits $0\le a_j<s_j$.

crt-map.name: axis coordinate
crt-map.meaning: The coordinate along axis i of the image of x^k.
crt-map.quote: The axis-$i$ coordinate $b_i$ of $\Phi(x^k)$ is $\mu_ik\bmod s_i$.

crt-map.name: address bits
crt-map.meaning: The number of address bits of an axis of length r.
crt-map.quote: Pad axis $i$ with zero records to a length $t_i$, a power of two with $r/2\le t_i\le r$, where $r=2^\ell$ and $\ell$ is the number of address bits of an axis of length $r$.

crt-map.name: padded record count
crt-map.meaning: The number of padded records, the product of the padded axis lengths.
crt-map.quote: Let $T=\prod_it_i$ be the number of padded records, each of $O(p)$ bits.

crt-map.name: interchange exponent
crt-map.meaning: A fixed exponent below 1 in the cost of the chunk interchange.

crt-map.name: address width
crt-map.meaning: The number of address bits of each of two equal-width axes being interchanged.
crt-map.quote: A [chunk interchange](address-interchange.md) exchanges two axes of equal address width $L$ in $O(VL^\tau)$ time

crt-map.name: padded axis length
crt-map.meaning: The length of axis i after padding with zero records, a power of two between r/2 and r.
crt-map.quote: Pad axis $i$ with zero records to a length $t_i$, a power of two with $r/2\le t_i\le r$, where $r=2^\ell$ and $\ell$ is the number of address bits of an axis of length $r$.

dft.name: sequence length
dft.meaning: The number of entries of a sequence.
dft.quote: Let $q\ge 1$ be the number of entries of a sequence, and let $u=(u_0,\dots,u_{q-1})$ be a sequence of $q$ complex numbers, with subscripts taken modulo $q$.

dft.name: input sequence
dft.meaning: A sequence of q complex numbers.
dft.quote: Let $q\ge 1$ be the number of entries of a sequence, and let $u=(u_0,\dots,u_{q-1})$ be a sequence of $q$ complex numbers, with subscripts taken modulo $q$.

dft.name: primitive root
dft.meaning: The primitive q-th root of unity e^{2 pi i/q}.
dft.quote: Writing $\omega = e^{2\pi i/q}$ for the primitive $q$-th root of unity, the weights are $\omega^{-jk}$; the opposite transform $F_q^+$ uses $\omega^{+jk}$.

dft.name: second sequence
dft.meaning: A second sequence of length q (not an integer input).
dft.quote: For sequences $u,v$ of length $q$, write $(u*v)_k=\sum_j u_j v_{k-j}$.

exchange-network.name: first data bank
exchange-network.meaning: One of the two data banks, with entries X_a.
exchange-network.quote: There are two data banks $X=(X_a)$ and $Y=(Y_a)$, indexed by $a\in\mathcal T^3$ ($a$ here is a triple of triples, not a shift exponent).

exchange-network.name: second data bank
exchange-network.meaning: The other data bank, with entries Y_a.
exchange-network.quote: There are two data banks $X=(X_a)$ and $Y=(Y_a)$, indexed by $a\in\mathcal T^3$ ($a$ here is a triple of triples, not a shift exponent).

exchange-network.name: bank index
exchange-network.meaning: A triple of three-element subsets of [h] indexing the entries of the banks.
exchange-network.quote: There are two data banks $X=(X_a)$ and $Y=(Y_a)$, indexed by $a\in\mathcal T^3$ ($a$ here is a triple of triples, not a shift exponent).

exchange-network.name: ground-set size
exchange-network.meaning: The size of the ground set [h] whose three-element subsets index the banks.
exchange-network.quote: Fix the ground-set size $h=100$ and write $[h]=\{1,\dots,h\}$.

exchange-network.name: triple set
exchange-network.meaning: The set of three-element subsets of [h].
exchange-network.quote: Let $\mathcal T$ be the set of three-element subsets of $[h]$, so that $v=\binom h3=161700$ counts them.

exchange-network.name: number of triples
exchange-network.meaning: The number of three-element subsets of [h].
exchange-network.quote: Let $\mathcal T$ be the set of three-element subsets of $[h]$, so that $v=\binom h3=161700$ counts them.

exchange-network.name: bank size
exchange-network.meaning: The number of values in each data bank.
exchange-network.quote: Set $N=v^3=4227952113000000$ for the size of each bank, and $m=h^3=1000000$ for the dimension of the label space used later.

exchange-network.name: label-space dimension
exchange-network.meaning: The dimension of the label space used on later pages.
exchange-network.quote: Set $N=v^3=4227952113000000$ for the size of each bank, and $m=h^3=1000000$ for the dimension of the label space used later.

exchange-network.name: invocation count
exchange-network.meaning: The number of invocations over all three stages.
exchange-network.quote: A stage covers all $v^2$ choices of the other two coordinates, each with its own invocation and scratch wires, so there are $I=3v^2=78440670000$ invocations.

exchange-network.name: bit neighbour count
exchange-network.meaning: The number of neighbours of a fixed triple in the bit construction.
exchange-network.quote: A triple has $z_{\rm b}=3\binom{97}{2}=13968$ neighbours in the bit construction

exchange-network.name: complex neighbour count
exchange-network.meaning: The number of neighbours of a fixed triple in the complex construction.
exchange-network.quote: It has $z_{\rm c}=\binom{97}{3}+3\cdot97=147731$ neighbours in the complex construction (intersection zero plus two)

exchange-network.name: bit central wires
exchange-network.meaning: The number of central wires per invocation in the bit network.
exchange-network.quote: There are $c_{\rm b}=100$ central wires per invocation in the bit network and $c_{\rm c}=101$ in the complex one.

exchange-network.name: complex central wires
exchange-network.meaning: The number of central wires per invocation in the complex network.
exchange-network.quote: There are $c_{\rm b}=100$ central wires per invocation in the bit network and $c_{\rm c}=101$ in the complex one.

exchange-network.name: bit wire count
exchange-network.meaning: The total number of wires in the bit network.
exchange-network.quote: The bit network has $W_{\rm b}=2N+I(vz_{\rm b}+c_{\rm b})=177176569091445000000$ wires

exchange-network.name: complex wire count
exchange-network.meaning: The total number of wires in the complex network.
exchange-network.quote: The complex network has $W_{\rm c}=2N+I(vz_{\rm c}+c_{\rm c})=1873807244643542670000$ wires

fixed-point.name: fractional bits
fixed-point.meaning: The number of fractional bits of the grid on which stored values lie.
fixed-point.quote: Let $p$ be the number of fractional bits, so stored values lie on the grid $2^{-p}\mathbb Z[i]$.

fixed-point.name: depth
fixed-point.meaning: The number of operations in sequence since the layer began that produced a value.
fixed-point.quote: Let a value computed with $k$ operations in sequence since the layer began be said to have depth $k$.

fixed-point.name: reserved extra bits
fixed-point.meaning: The number of extra bits reserved, at least the maximal depth reached in the layer.
fixed-point.quote: Let $\Delta$ be the number of extra bits reserved, at least the maximal depth reached in the layer.

fixed-point.name: truncation
fixed-point.meaning: The truncation that drops the bits below 2^{-p} in each real and imaginary part, returning a record to the p-bit grid.
fixed-point.quote: The truncation $Q_p$ drops the bits below $2^{-p}$ in each real and imaginary part, returning the record to the $p$-bit grid, with error below $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$ per complex coefficient.

frequency-order.name: round count
frequency-order.meaning: The number of rounds of the transform, a=log_2 t.
frequency-order.quote: put $a=\log_2t$, the number of rounds (here $a$ changes meaning)

frequency-order.name: output index
frequency-order.meaning: The position of an output of the transform.
frequency-order.quote: with input positions $k$ and output index $j$ (here $j$ changes meaning: it is the position of an output of the transform)

frequency-order.name: completed rounds
frequency-order.meaning: The number of rounds completed so far.
frequency-order.quote: After $s$ rounds, $s$ being the number of completed rounds, slots $a-1,\dots,a-s$ hold frequency bits $0,\dots,s-1$ and the rest index a sequence of length $t/2^s$; the next round writes bit $s$ into slot $a-1-s$.

frequency-order.name: bit-reversal permutation
frequency-order.meaning: The permutation moving the entry at j to rev_a(j).
frequency-order.quote: Let $B_t$ be the permutation moving the entry at $j$ to $\operatorname{rev}_a(j)$

frequency-order.name: parallel butterfly
frequency-order.meaning: The parallel butterfly applying H_0 on every participating axis in one round.
frequency-order.quote: With several axes, indexed by $i$, a round applies $H_0$ on every participating axis, and $\mathcal H$ denotes this one parallel butterfly.

frequency-order.name: recordwise monomial
frequency-order.meaning: The recordwise operation multiplying each record by y^E.
frequency-order.quote: Twiddles group into one monomial $J_E$, the recordwise operation multiplying the record by $y^E$, where $E$ depends on the address, not coefficients:

gaussian-resampling.name: source length
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The number of entries of the sequence whose transform is re-expressed.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Gaussian resampling expresses the Fourier transform of a source length $s$ through the transform of a nearby larger power-of-two length $t$, so that only power-of-two transforms need a fast algorithm.

gaussian-resampling.name: length gap
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The relative gap t/s-1 between the padded and source lengths.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Assume $\theta:=t/s-1>p/\alpha^4$.

gaussian-resampling.name: source permutation
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The coordinate permutation (P_s u)_j = u_{tj} of length-s vectors.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Define the permutations $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ and $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$, with indices taken modulo $s$ and $t$.

gaussian-resampling.name: target permutation
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The coordinate permutation (P_t v)_k = v_{-sk} of length-t vectors.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Define the permutations $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ and $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$, with indices taken modulo $s$ and $t$.

gaussian-resampling.name: input contraction

gaussian-resampling.name: output contraction

gaussian-resampling.name: nearest index

gaussian-resampling.name: rounding offset

gaussian-resampling.name: coordinate selection

parameter-choice.quote: In the [simultaneous butterfly layer](simultaneous-layer.md), $\tau$ is the exponent in the cost of a chunk interchange, $\sigma$ bounds the growth exponent of recursive calls, $\beta$ sets the threshold $d^\beta$ below which active chunks are handled singly, $\lambda$ is the per-node overhead exponent, $\lambda'$ is the final exponent of the cost $Vd^{\lambda'}$ (up to a constant) on bit volume $V$, $c$ is the exponent of the address-chunk width (here it is not the scaling integer of [Controlled shifts and rational scalings](controlled-shifts.md)), $\epsilon$ is the exponent of the axis count, $C_1$ is the exponent of the guard bits, and $\delta$ is the resampling-cost slack.

parameter-choice.name: bit volume
parameter-choice.meaning: The number of stored bits on which the layer cost is measured.
parameter-choice.quote: In the [simultaneous butterfly layer](simultaneous-layer.md), $\tau$ is the exponent in the cost of a chunk interchange, $\sigma$ bounds the growth exponent of recursive calls, $\beta$ sets the threshold $d^\beta$ below which active chunks are handled singly, $\lambda$ is the per-node overhead exponent, $\lambda'$ is the final exponent of the cost $Vd^{\lambda'}$ (up to a constant) on bit volume $V$, $c$ is the exponent of the address-chunk width (here it is not the scaling integer of [Controlled shifts and rational scalings](controlled-shifts.md)), $\epsilon$ is the exponent of the axis count, $C_1$ is the exponent of the guard bits, and $\delta$ is the resampling-cost slack.

parameter-choice.name: chunk width
parameter-choice.meaning: The width in bits of an address chunk.
parameter-choice.quote: Put $K=\lfloor d^c\rfloor$, the width in bits of an address chunk.

parameter-choice.name: prime gap fraction
parameter-choice.meaning: The smallest relative distance at which a prime s_i may lie below t_i.
parameter-choice.quote: Put $\gamma=2d\alpha^2$ and $\eta=1/(4d)$, where $\gamma$ is the exponent of the scale factor $2^\gamma$ of $d$-axis resampling, and $\eta$ is the smallest relative distance at which a prime $s_i$ may lie below $t_i$.

phase-frames.name: binary vector
phase-frames.meaning: A binary vector in F_2^m (not the number of triples).
phase-frames.quote: Here $v$ is a binary vector, not the number of triples on the exchange-network page.

phase-frames.name: edge residual
phase-frames.meaning: The edge residual of an edge: the orthogonal summand added going from U to V (not a tensor factor).
phase-frames.quote: Here $E$ is an edge residual, not the first tensor factor on the tensor-product page.

phase-frames.name: column count
phase-frames.meaning: The number of columns of data, so that an address is a k-tuple (not a depth).
phase-frames.quote: Here $k$ counts columns of data, not the depth on the fixed-point page.

phase-frames.name: binary vector
phase-frames.meaning: A binary vector in F_2^m (not an input sequence).
phase-frames.quote: Here $u$ is a binary vector, not the input sequence on the discrete Fourier transform page.

phase-frames.name: binary vector
phase-frames.quote: Labels are subspaces of $\mathbb F_2^m$ ($m$ the label dimension), and $u,v,w,z$ are vectors of $\mathbb F_2^m$ here.

phase-frames.name: binary vector
phase-frames.quote: Labels are subspaces of $\mathbb F_2^m$ ($m$ the label dimension), and $u,v,w,z$ are vectors of $\mathbb F_2^m$ here.

phase-frames.name: support
phase-frames.meaning: The set of coordinates where a binary vector is 1.
phase-frames.quote: The support $\operatorname{supp}(z)$ of a vector is the set of coordinates where it is $1$.

phase-frames.name: Hamming weight
phase-frames.meaning: The Hamming weight: the number of coordinates where a binary vector is 1.
phase-frames.quote: Write $\operatorname{wt}(x)=|\operatorname{supp}(x)|$ for the Hamming weight, $[b]\in\{0,1\}$ for the integer representative of $b\in\mathbb F_2$, $P_U$ for projection onto a label $U$, and $z\cdot w$ for the dot product, both over $\mathbb F_2$.

phase-frames.name: projection
phase-frames.meaning: The projection onto a label U over F_2.
phase-frames.quote: Write $\operatorname{wt}(x)=|\operatorname{supp}(x)|$ for the Hamming weight, $[b]\in\{0,1\}$ for the integer representative of $b\in\mathbb F_2$, $P_U$ for projection onto a label $U$, and $z\cdot w$ for the dot product, both over $\mathbb F_2$.

phase-frames.name: translation by v
phase-frames.meaning: The translation of functions of x by the binary vector v.
phase-frames.quote: Let $X_v$ be the translation $(X_vf)(x)=f(x+v)$, and $C=H\operatorname{diag}(1,i)H=aI+bX$ with $a=\frac{1+i}{2}$, $b=\frac{1-i}{2}$, where $H=\tfrac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}$.

phase-frames.name: weight phase exponent
phase-frames.meaning: The Hamming weight of P_U x, modulo four.
phase-frames.quote: For a label $U$ put $q_U(x)=\operatorname{wt}(P_Ux)\bmod 4$, with the projection taken over $\mathbb F_2$.

phase-frames.name: phase frame
phase-frames.meaning: The phase frame of the label U.
phase-frames.quote: The phase frame is $\mathcal C_U=H^{\otimes m}\operatorname{diag}_x(i^{q_U(x)})H^{\otimes m}$, with Gaussian-dyadic entries.

phase-frames.name: orthonormal basis
phase-frames.meaning: An orthonormal basis of the edge residual E.
phase-frames.quote: Take an edge from $U$ to $V=U\perp E$, where $E$, the edge residual, has orthonormal basis $\mathcal B$.

phase-frames.name: edge phase sign
phase-frames.meaning: The sign, plus or minus one modulo four, of one basis vector's phase term, including the edge direction.
phase-frames.quote: Each term is therefore $\varepsilon[v\cdot x]$ with $\varepsilon=\pm1$ modulo four, the sign including the edge direction.

phase-frames.name: sign matrix
phase-frames.quote: With $Z=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$ we have $ZXZ=-X$ and $C^{-1}=bI+aX$; since $ib=a$ and $ia=-b$, $C=iZC^{-1}Z$.

phase-frames.name: sign operator
phase-frames.meaning: Z on the 27 coordinates of supp(u) in every column, the identity elsewhere.
phase-frames.quote: Let $Z_{a,k}$ be $Z$ on those 27 coordinates in every column.

phase-kernel.name: identity matrix
phase-kernel.quote: Let $I$ be the $2\times 2$ identity matrix, and let $X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ be the bit flip, which swaps the two entries of a pair $(u,v)$.

phase-kernel.name: bit flip
phase-kernel.meaning: The 2x2 matrix swapping the two entries of a pair.
phase-kernel.quote: Let $I$ be the $2\times 2$ identity matrix, and let $X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ be the bit flip, which swaps the two entries of a pair $(u,v)$.

phase-kernel.name: kernel constant
phase-kernel.quote: Let $a=\frac{1+i}{2}$ be a complex constant, which is not a bank index.

phase-kernel.name: kernel coefficient
phase-kernel.meaning: The complex coefficient (1-i)/2 of the bit flip in the kernel.
phase-kernel.quote: Let $b=\frac{1-i}{2}$ be the kernel coefficient, which here is not the lowest bit of the output index as on the butterfly page.

phase-kernel.name: phase matrix
phase-kernel.meaning: The diagonal matrix diag(1, i) multiplying the second entry of a pair by i.
phase-kernel.quote: Let $\mathsf S=\operatorname{diag}(1,i)$ be the phase matrix that multiplies the second entry of a pair by $i$.

phase-kernel.name: averaging step
phase-kernel.meaning: The matrix of the two-point averaging and differencing step.
phase-kernel.quote: Let $H_0=\frac12\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}$ be the matrix of the averaging and differencing step $(u,v)\mapsto\bigl(\tfrac{u+v}{2},\tfrac{u-v}{2}\bigr)$, and let $H=\sqrt2\,H_0$ be the normalized Hadamard matrix, which is symmetric and satisfies $H^2=I$.

phase-kernel.name: Hadamard matrix
phase-kernel.meaning: The normalized Hadamard matrix sqrt(2) H_0.
phase-kernel.quote: Let $H_0=\frac12\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}$ be the matrix of the averaging and differencing step $(u,v)\mapsto\bigl(\tfrac{u+v}{2},\tfrac{u-v}{2}\bigr)$, and let $H=\sqrt2\,H_0$ be the normalized Hadamard matrix, which is symmetric and satisfies $H^2=I$.

phase-twist.name: axis count
phase-twist.meaning: The number of axes of the arrays f and g.
phase-twist.quote: Let $f$ and $g$ be complex arrays with $d$ axes, the last of length $r$, and $T$ entries in all.

phase-twist.name: first array
phase-twist.meaning: A complex array with d axes, the last of length r.
phase-twist.quote: Let $f$ and $g$ be complex arrays with $d$ axes, the last of length $r$, and $T$ entries in all.

phase-twist.name: second array
phase-twist.meaning: The second complex array, with the same shape as f.
phase-twist.quote: Let $f$ and $g$ be complex arrays with $d$ axes, the last of length $r$, and $T$ entries in all.

phase-twist.name: last axis variable
phase-twist.meaning: The variable of the last cyclic axis.
phase-twist.quote: But convolution along it is multiplication in $\mathbb C[x_d]/(x_d^r-1)$, where $x_d$ is the variable of that axis and the wrap is cyclic, whereas in $\mathcal R_r$ the wrap changes sign.

phase-twist.name: negacyclic ring
phase-twist.meaning: The ring of polynomials in y modulo y^r+1 over the complex numbers.
phase-twist.quote: The fast convolution of the later stages, [Convolution from the retained transform layout](ring-convolution.md), convolves the first $d-1$ axes of an array whose entries are records in $\mathcal R_r=\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$.

phase-twist.name: twist phase
phase-twist.meaning: The complex number e^{\pi i/r}, with \zeta^r=-1.

phase-twist.name: twist map
phase-twist.meaning: The ring isomorphism from C[x_d]/(x_d^r-1) to R_r sending x_d to \zeta y.

phase-twist.name: coefficient index
phase-twist.meaning: The index of a coefficient along the last axis (here not a depth).
phase-twist.quote: Here $k$ and $l$ index coefficients along the last axis (not depth).

phase-twist.name: second coefficient index
phase-twist.meaning: The index of a second coefficient along the last axis.
phase-twist.quote: Here $k$ and $l$ index coefficients along the last axis (not depth).

phase-twist.name: wrapped position
phase-twist.meaning: The position in 0..r-1 of a product term after reduction.
phase-twist.quote: Take $k,l<r$ and write $k+l=j+hr$, with $j<r$ the resulting position and $h\in\{0,1\}$ the wrap indicator.

phase-twist.name: wrap indicator
phase-twist.meaning: Zero or one, the number of times the index k+l wraps past r.
phase-twist.quote: Take $k,l<r$ and write $k+l=j+hr$, with $j<r$ the resulting position and $h\in\{0,1\}$ the wrap indicator.

phase-twist.name: line count
phase-twist.meaning: The number of lines along the last axis, T/r.
phase-twist.quote: Then $M=T/r$ is the number of lines along the last axis.

phase-twist.name: line-to-record map
phase-twist.meaning: Reads each line along the last axis as a polynomial in y, giving an array of M records in R_r.
phase-twist.quote: Let $\iota$ read each line $(f_{\boldsymbol j,k})_k$ as the polynomial $\sum_k f_{\boldsymbol j,k}y^k$, giving an array of $M$ records in $\mathcal R_r$, and let $(D_\pm f)_{\boldsymbol j,k}=\zeta^{\pm k}f_{\boldsymbol j,k}$ multiply entry $k$ of each line by $\zeta^{\pm k}$.

phase-twist.name: twist and untwist
phase-twist.meaning: Multiplication of entry k of each line by \zeta^{\pm k}.
phase-twist.quote: Let $\iota$ read each line $(f_{\boldsymbol j,k})_k$ as the polynomial $\sum_k f_{\boldsymbol j,k}y^k$, giving an array of $M$ records in $\mathcal R_r$, and let $(D_\pm f)_{\boldsymbol j,k}=\zeta^{\pm k}f_{\boldsymbol j,k}$ multiply entry $k$ of each line by $\zeta^{\pm k}$.

phase-twist.name: ring convolution
phase-twist.meaning: The normalized convolution of the first d-1 axes over R_r, dividing by T.
phase-twist.quote: Let $\mathcal M_r$ be the ring convolution: it convolves the first $d-1$ axes over $\mathcal R_r$, dividing by $T$.

phase-twist.name: complex convolution
phase-twist.meaning: The normalized complex cyclic convolution, equal to f*g/T.
phase-twist.quote: The normalized complex cyclic convolution $\mathcal M_{\mathbb C}$ is

phase-twist.name: sup norm
phase-twist.meaning: The largest modulus of a scalar coefficient of f.
phase-twist.quote: Let $\|f\|$ be the sup norm of $f$, the largest modulus of a scalar coefficient.

precision-recovery.name: grid spacing
precision-recovery.meaning: The grid spacing 2^{-p} of the fixed-point records.
precision-recovery.quote: Write $h_p=2^{-p}$ and $L=\log_2T$, the base-2 logarithm of the padded length $T$ (the letter $L$ here is not a linear map as on the contractions page).

precision-recovery.name: log of padded length
precision-recovery.meaning: The base-2 logarithm of the padded length T.
precision-recovery.quote: Write $h_p=2^{-p}$ and $L=\log_2T$, the base-2 logarithm of the padded length $T$ (the letter $L$ here is not a linear map as on the contractions page).

precision-recovery.name: error size
precision-recovery.meaning: The size of an error in grid spacings.
precision-recovery.quote: Norms are sup norms, an error of $a$ means error below $ah_p$ (here $a$ is an error size in grid spacings, not the chirp), and every array stays in the unit disk (norm $\le1$).

precision-recovery.name: disk array
precision-recovery.meaning: An array in the unit disk to which a phase or chirp transform is applied.
precision-recovery.quote: For a unit phase $e$, an approximation $\widetilde e$ with $|\widetilde e-e|<2h_p$ and a disk operand $x$ (here $x$ is an array in the unit disk to which a phase or chirp transform is applied, not the polynomial variable), the product differs by under $2\|x\|h_p$ and truncation $Q_p$ adds under $\sqrt2h_p$, so $\|Q_p(\widetilde ex)-ex\|<(2\|x\|+\sqrt2)h_p<4h_p$.

precision-recovery.name: scaled first digits
precision-recovery.meaning: The scaled digit array of the first input.
precision-recovery.quote: Now $u,v$ are the scaled digit arrays of the two inputs, not the input integers of the radix-digit page: each digit is stored as its value times $2^{-b-2}$, so norms are below $1/4$.

precision-recovery.name: scaled second digits
precision-recovery.meaning: The scaled digit array of the second input.
precision-recovery.quote: Now $u,v$ are the scaled digit arrays of the two inputs, not the input integers of the radix-digit page: each digit is stored as its value times $2^{-b-2}$, so norms are below $1/4$.

radix-digit-reduction.name: first input
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The first of the two n-bit integers being multiplied.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Call the two inputs $u$ and $u'$, each with $n$ bits.

radix-digit-reduction.name: second input
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The second of the two n-bit integers being multiplied.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Call the two inputs $u$ and $u'$, each with $n$ bits.

radix-digit-reduction.name: digit bits
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The number of bits in one radix-2^b digit.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Let $b=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$ be the number of bits in one digit, so $n\le 2^b$.

radix-digit-reduction.name: convolution length
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The length of the cyclic convolution, between T/2 and T, a product of distinct odd primes.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: $S$ is the length of the cyclic convolution, with $T/2<S<T$.

radix-digit-reduction.name: polynomial variable
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The variable of the digit polynomials, evaluated at 2^b to recover the integers.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Let $x$ be a polynomial variable, and form the polynomials in $x$ with the $u_i$ and with the $u'_k$ as coefficients.

radix-digit-reduction.name: digit of u
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The i-th radix-2^b digit of u, an integer from 0 to 2^b-1.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Write $u=\sum_{i=0}^{q-1}u_i2^{bi}$ and $u'=\sum_{k=0}^{q-1}u'_k2^{bk}$, where the digits $u_i$ and $u'_k$ are integers with $0\le u_i,u'_k<2^b$.

radix-digit-reduction.name: digit of u'
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The k-th radix-2^b digit of u', an integer from 0 to 2^b-1.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Write $u=\sum_{i=0}^{q-1}u_i2^{bi}$ and $u'=\sum_{k=0}^{q-1}u'_k2^{bk}$, where the digits $u_i$ and $u'_k$ are integers with $0\le u_i,u'_k<2^b$.

radix-digit-reduction.name: product coefficient
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The coefficient of x^j in the product of the two digit polynomials.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Let $c_j=\sum_{i+k=j}u_iu'_k$ be the coefficient of $x^j$ in that product.

radix-digit-reduction.name: padded length
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The number of coefficients of the padded array, a power of two between 4n/b and 8n/b.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: $T$ is a power of two with $4n/b\le T<8n/b$, the size of the padded array on which the later power-of-two transforms act.

radix-digit-reduction.name: digit count
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The number of radix-2^b digits in each input.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Let $q=\lceil n/b\rceil$ be the number of digits in each input, padding with leading zeros.

rank-recurrence.name: call parameter
rank-recurrence.meaning: The parameter of a recursive call: the number of digits per interchanged chunk, or the number of selected axes of a layer.
rank-recurrence.quote: A call acts on a stream of volume $V$ and has a parameter $f$ (a number here, not an array): the digits per interchanged chunk, or the selected axes of a layer.

rank-recurrence.name: time per unit volume
rank-recurrence.meaning: The running time of a call at a given parameter, divided by the volume of its stream.
rank-recurrence.quote: Let $\mathcal C(f)$ be the time per unit volume of a call at parameter $f$: its running time divided by its stream's volume.

rank-recurrence.name: recursion depth
rank-recurrence.meaning: The number of recursion levels below the top call, indexing the terms of the unrolled sum; here not a stage number.
rank-recurrence.quote: Unrolling $\log_m f$ levels, depth $j$ (the number of levels below the top call, not a stage number) contributes $(s/W)^j$, so $\mathcal C(f)=O\big(\sum_{j=0}^{\log_m f}(s/W)^j\big)$.

rank-recurrence.name: relative rank deficit
rank-recurrence.meaning: The relative amount (Wm-s)/(Wm) by which the number of smaller calls falls short of Wm; here not the prime distance of the parameter-choice page.
rank-recurrence.quote: Write $s/W=m(1-\eta)$, with $\eta$ here the relative deficit $(Wm-s)/(Wm)$, not the prime distance of [Parameter and prime-length choice](parameter-choice.md).

retained-permutations.name: source entry count
retained-permutations.meaning: The number of entries of the source array, the product of the source axis lengths.
retained-permutations.quote: Write $\boldsymbol s=(s_1,\dots,s_d)$, $\boldsymbol t=(t_1,\dots,t_d)$, $S=\prod_is_i$ (the number of entries of the source array) and $T=\prod_it_i$ (the number of entries of the padded box).

retained-permutations.name: padded entry count
retained-permutations.meaning: The number of entries of the padded box, the product of the padded axis lengths.
retained-permutations.quote: Write $\boldsymbol s=(s_1,\dots,s_d)$, $\boldsymbol t=(t_1,\dots,t_d)$, $S=\prod_is_i$ (the number of entries of the source array) and $T=\prod_it_i$ (the number of entries of the padded box).

retained-permutations.name: source permutation
retained-permutations.meaning: The tensor product of the source axis permutations; it is a permutation, not the scalar ring.
retained-permutations.quote: Put $R=\bigotimes_iP_{s_i}$ (the source permutation, not a ring), $Q=\bigotimes_iP_{t_i}$, $\mathcal A=\bigotimes_iA_i$, $\mathcal B_0=\bigotimes_iB_{0,i}$.

retained-permutations.name: output map
retained-permutations.meaning: The linear contraction applied after the power-of-two transform in the one-axis resampling identity; unrelated to the packing base.
retained-permutations.quote: The resampling page gives linear contractions $A$ and $B_0$, the input and output maps ($B_0$ is unrelated to the packing base of [signed packing](signed-packing.md)), with $P_sF_s=2^{2\alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA$, computed in time $O(tp^{3/2+\delta}\alpha)$ without executing $P_s$ or $P_t$.

retained-permutations.name: unit
retained-permutations.meaning: A unit modulo q, used to define the index permutation R_beta.
retained-permutations.quote: For a unit $\beta$ modulo $q$ let $(R_\beta z)_j=z_{\beta j}$.

retained-permutations.name: summation index
retained-permutations.meaning: The index of summation in the Fourier sum.
retained-permutations.quote: Then $(F_q^+R_\beta z)_j=\frac1q\sum_w z_{\beta w}e^{2\pi i wj/q}$, with $w$ the summation index.

retained-permutations.name: setup exponent
retained-permutations.meaning: A fixed exponent such that the setup work per line is O(p^nu).
retained-permutations.quote:
Since $t_i\ge r/2$, each tensor map invokes at most $\sum_iT/t_i\le 2dT/r$ lines, so a setup of $O(p^
u)$ per line, with $
u$ a fixed exponent, totals $O(dTp^
u/r)$.

retained-permutations.name: first array
retained-permutations.meaning: A complex array, not an integer being multiplied.
retained-permutations.quote: For one axis, with $\alpha$ and $\delta$ as on the resampling page, let $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ and $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$, where $u$ and $v$ are complex arrays here, not the integers being multiplied.

retained-permutations.name: second array
retained-permutations.meaning: A complex array, not an integer being multiplied.
retained-permutations.quote: For one axis, with $\alpha$ and $\delta$ as on the resampling page, let $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ and $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$, where $u$ and $v$ are complex arrays here, not the integers being multiplied.

ring-convolution.name: output position
ring-convolution.meaning: A position in the cyclic axes, with components j_i, labelling an entry of the transform.
ring-convolution.quote: Tuples $\boldsymbol j,\boldsymbol k,\boldsymbol l$ are positions in the cyclic axes, with components $j_i,k_i,l_i$.

ring-convolution.name: first input position
ring-convolution.meaning: A position in the cyclic axes, with components k_i.
ring-convolution.quote: Tuples $\boldsymbol j,\boldsymbol k,\boldsymbol l$ are positions in the cyclic axes, with components $j_i,k_i,l_i$.

ring-convolution.name: second input position
ring-convolution.meaning: A position in the cyclic axes, with components l_i.
ring-convolution.quote: Tuples $\boldsymbol j,\boldsymbol k,\boldsymbol l$ are positions in the cyclic axes, with components $j_i,k_i,l_i$.

ring-convolution.name: power-of-y root
ring-convolution.meaning: The power y^{2r/t} of y, playing the role of a t-th root of unity.
ring-convolution.quote: Put $\omega_t=y^{2r/t}$, a power of $y$ that plays a $t$-th root of unity, and $\chi_{\boldsymbol j}(\boldsymbol k)=\prod_i\omega_{t_i}^{-j_ik_i}$.

ring-convolution.name: transform character
ring-convolution.meaning: The product over axes of omega_{t_i}^{-j_i k_i}, a power of y.
ring-convolution.quote: Put $\omega_t=y^{2r/t}$, a power of $y$ that plays a $t$-th root of unity, and $\chi_{\boldsymbol j}(\boldsymbol k)=\prod_i\omega_{t_i}^{-j_ik_i}$.

ring-convolution.name: pointwise product
ring-convolution.meaning: The record-by-record product P(u,v)=uv/r of two arrays over the ring.

ring-convolution.name: transform error
ring-convolution.meaning: The error bound sqrt2 * l * 2^{-p} of each transform procedure.
ring-convolution.quote: Put $\delta=\sqrt2\ell\,2^{-p}$ for the error of each transform procedure and $\eta=\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$ for one truncation $Q_p$.

ring-convolution.name: truncation error
ring-convolution.meaning: The error bound sqrt2 * 2^{-p} of one truncation Q_p.
ring-convolution.quote: Put $\delta=\sqrt2\ell\,2^{-p}$ for the error of each transform procedure and $\eta=\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$ for one truncation $Q_p$.

ring-y.name: ring variable
ring-y.meaning: The indeterminate of the polynomials; it satisfies y^r = -1 in the ring.
ring-y.quote: Write $\mathcal R_r=\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$ for it, where $y$ is the ring variable, the indeterminate of the polynomials, and $r$ is the record length, the number of complex coefficients in a polynomial of the ring, always a power of two with $r\geq 2$.

ring-y.name: record length
ring-y.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in a polynomial of the ring, always a power of two.
ring-y.quote: Write $\mathcal R_r=\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$ for it, where $y$ is the ring variable, the indeterminate of the polynomials, and $r$ is the record length, the number of complex coefficients in a polynomial of the ring, always a power of two with $r\geq 2$.

signed-packing.name: packing base
signed-packing.meaning: The base 2^{4p} at which the polynomials are evaluated.

signed-packing.name: signed evaluation integer
signed-packing.meaning: The integer obtained by evaluating the integer-coefficient polynomial u at B_0.
signed-packing.quote: let $A_u=u(B_0)=\sum_{j<r}u_jB_0^j$ be the signed evaluation integer

signed-packing.name: carry
signed-packing.meaning: The carry, in {-1,0}, into block j when forming A_u.
signed-packing.quote: scan the coefficients with a carry $\gamma_j$

signed-packing.name: block
signed-packing.meaning: The residue of u_j plus the carry modulo B_0, the j-th block of 4p bits of A_u.
signed-packing.quote: Let $d_j\in[0,B_0)$ be the residue of $u_j+\gamma_j$ modulo $B_0$

signed-packing.name: product coefficient
signed-packing.meaning: The coefficient of y^j in the ordinary product h=ac of integer polynomials.

signed-packing.name: extraction carry
signed-packing.meaning: The carry into block j during extraction, in {0,1}.
signed-packing.quote: let $\rho_j$ be the carry into block $j$

signed-packing.name: reduced coefficient
signed-packing.meaning: The Gaussian integer coefficient of y^j after reduction modulo y^r+1.
signed-packing.quote: Let $H_j$ be the resulting Gaussian integer coefficient.

simultaneous-layer.name: selected chunk count

main-result.quote: Power-saving integer multiplication is the main result: for $n$, the number of bits in each input, and $\kappa=2^{-182}$, the exponent saved from the power of $\lg n$, one fixed Turing machine multiplies two $n$-bit integers exactly in time $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$, which is $o(n\log n)$, so it refutes the [Schönhage–Strassen optimality conjecture](conjecture.md) in this model.

The exact $2n$-bit product is assembled by [The multiplication algorithm](multiplication-algorithm.md) from radix digits, two forward transforms, a pointwise product, the opposite transform, rescaling, rounding and carries, with total error below $1/2$.

The running time is totalled by [Cost accounting and the exponent κ](cost-accounting.md) after dividing every cost by $V=Tp=\Theta(n)$, where $T$ counts the complex coefficients and $p$, of order $\lg n$, is the number of fractional bits of each.

multidim-transform.quote: Both maps are contractions, so each has input errors bounded as in [Contractions and bilinear contractions](contraction-maps.md).

multiplication-algorithm.quote: It takes its sizes from [Parameter and prime-length choice](parameter-choice.md): $b=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$ bits per radix digit, $p=6b$ fractional bits for every stored value, distinct odd primes $s_i$ with product $S$, and powers of two $t_i$ just above $s_i$ with product $T$.
